mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Particulars)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy from registry -> notarization by Korean notary public -> Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Hague Apostille Convention destination countries; for non-Hague destinations, notarization -> consular legalization by the destination country's embassy/consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original tax clearance certificate -> notarization -> Apostille by MOFA for Hague member states; parallel notarization -> consular legalization by destination non-Hague consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders' board, notarized by Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution in front of Korean notary -> Apostille by MOFA for Hague member states; parallel non-Hague path: execution before notary -> consular legalization by destination consulate in Seoul. Do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation / Jeonggwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of Korean Articles -> Apostille by MOFA for Hague states; for non-Hague states, notarization -> consular legalization by the destination state's consulate. The two authentication regimes are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Korean commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank after entity bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued reference letter -> bank officer signature and seal -> notarization -> Apostille by MOFA for Hague states; non-Hague states follow notarization -> consular legalization by destination consulate. Use only one path depending on destination membership.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before engagement, every shareholder, director, UBO, signatory, and material counterparty must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Consolidated Sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and Ministry of Foreign Affairs designations, and Interpol notices. Any current or former foreign PEP, family member, or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior compliance approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse media, sanctions exposure, or refusal to provide UBO information constitutes a disqualifying red flag.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) and Korea Intellectual Property Rights Information Service (KIPRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered statutory name must be written in Hangul and must end with the suffix '유한회사 (Yuhan Hoesa)'. A foreign-language trade name may be registered only as a secondary trade name; the primary legal name must comply with Hangul phonetic transliteration rules. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) KIPRIS trademark identical/similar check for both Hangul and English renderings; (2) IROS corporate-name duplicate check; (3) review of prohibited and sensitive tokens requiring ministerial approval; and (4) confirmation of mandatory suffix, capitalization and registered-office compatibility.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the registrar within 14 days, attaching evidence of trademark coexistence or ministerial approval. If the registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the district court under the Registration Examination Regulations within seven days. Counsel should simultaneously submit amended name alternatives to prevent restarting the statutory period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is acceptable only if the service provider operates a physical serviced office in Korea that can accept legal process, maintains a sublease in the company name, and provides meeting space and mail handling. Pure virtual addresses without staff or operational presence are rejected by Korean banks for corporate account opening, and the National Tax Service may reclassify the office as fictitious, denying VAT input credits and imposing penalties. For TikTok Shop retail and live-commerce fulfilment, the registered office must maintain at least contract files, e-commerce records, inventory or third-party fulfilment agreements, and a named local contact person.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) company nameplate at the registered office; (2) actual workstations and staff presence; (3) e-commerce transaction records and electronic tax invoices; (4) inventory, shipping, or third-party fulfilment contracts; (5) utility and internet contracts under the company name; (6) lease agreement in the company name; (7) director or appointed manager available during business hours. Quantified risk: 15% for a serviced office with local staff and complete records; 55% for a virtual office without dedicated staff; 80% for a pure mailbox address with no operational presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Chapter 2, Section 4, Articles 287-2 et seq. governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with the Commercial Registration Act and the Framework Act on Real Name Financial Transactions for the capital verification deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, with online filing through the Korean Supreme Court I-reg e-registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (Bupin Deungki Cheong-gu), attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), capital payment certificate, consent of officers, and court seal notification forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under Korean law. The contributed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be paid in full at establishment, and the funds must remain blocked in a domestic bank establishment deposit account until incorporation registration is completed; after registration, the funds may be withdrawn for lawful business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of KR YUHANGHOESA under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea be and it is hereby ratified, confirmed, and accepted by the Board of Directors; and that the total issued and subscribed contributed capital of the Company in the amount of KRW [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] transferable contribution units with a par or stated value of KRW [VALUE] each, be and hereby is subscribed, accepted, and treated as fully paid in cash, and the Board directs the representative director to deposit or cause to be deposited such capital in a domestic bank establishment deposit account and to obtain a capital payment certificate from such bank for filing with the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be located at [Registered Office Address], Republic of Korea, and that the Board approves the lease or service contract, the power of attorney to the licensed formation agent, and the use of such address for service and statutory notices; and that the representative director be and hereby is authorized to execute any document and to make any registration or amendment necessary to adopt, maintain, or move the registered office as required by the Commercial Act. RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors hereby authorizes the opening of one or more corporate operating accounts with a commercial bank licensed to do business in the Republic of Korea, including the TikTok Shop settlement account and cross-border payout rail with Wise B2B; and that the representative director, accompanied by one additional director or a staff signatory designated by the representative director, be and hereby is appointed as the authorized signatory with authority to instruct, transfer, withdraw, and manage funds, provided that any payment exceeding KRW 10,000,000 requires double authorization; and that the bank be, and it hereby is, authorized to rely on the certificate of incumbency and a copy of this resolution, and to change the mandate upon receipt of a subsequent resolution. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and hereby is appointed as the director and representative director of the Company, and that [Name] be and hereby is appointed as the director and auditor or internal control officer to the extent required by law; and that the representative director is authorized to apply for the corporate business registration with the National Tax Service, the communication-selling business report with the competent municipal authority, and all other licenses and regulatory filings incidental to the operation of an online social commerce platform, and to execute the TikTok Shop seller contract and payment service agreements in the Company name. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the initial organizers, formation agent, and any officer of the Company prior to this resolution are ratified; and that this resolution may be signed in counterparts and may be relied upon by banks, government agencies, tax authorities, and payment service providers as conclusive evidence of the Board authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Supreme Court I-reg e-registration portal for company name search; Korean Notary Public commissioned under the Notary Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the company name record maintained by the Supreme Court of Korea to confirm that the exact name KR YUHANGHOESA is distinguishable from existing registered commercial trade names. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation under the Commercial Act specifying the corporate name, business object, registered office location, contributed capital, number and par value of contribution units, contribution method, and the initial members and directors. The Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public. If any member is a corporation, attach an extract of its corporate registry and a power of attorney executed by its legal representative. After notarization, preserve the notarized original for submission to the Court Registry in Step 3.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan)
Planned corporate registered seal specimen
Individual seals and identification copies of members and directors
Corporate registry extract and power of attorney for any corporate member
Name search record or confirmation from I-reg portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is denied or a notary requests amendments, execute a corrected Articles of Incorporation and resubmit under the same application number. If a prior registrant objects, adopt a distinguishing modified English or Korean trade name and file again. Notary queries regarding signature authority are cured by supplying a fresh corporate registry extract and a notarized power of attorney within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Bank Verification Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank branch in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, or NH Nonghyup Bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate establishment deposit account in the planned corporate name with a Korean commercial bank. Pay in full the contributed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation from the personal or corporate account of each subscriber. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit for paid-up capital, which is mandatory for the Court Registry. The funds must remain blocked until the incorporation registration is completed. If non-cash contributions are intended, deliver the asset and obtain a valuation report from a qualified appraiser; for this social commerce entity, cash contribution is recommended to avoid registration complications.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Temporary deposit account application form
Capital payment certificate from the bank
Power of attorney if deposit is made by a third party
AML source-of-funds declaration
Passport or corporate registry extract for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to AML or KYC concerns, provide a notarized business plan, physical proof of location, and a detailed source-of-funds statement. If the capital payment certificate is later rejected by the Court Registry because of a name mismatch, request the bank to reissue the certificate in the exact registered name and provide a covering correction letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office, using the Korean Supreme Court I-reg electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal Application for Corporation Registration to the competent Court Registry. The application must comply with the Commercial Registration Act and include a statement confirming lawful establishment, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital payment certificate, written consents of the directors and members, and the registered seal notification form. The registry officer conducts a documentary legal audit and, if satisfied, assigns a commercial registration number and issues the certificate of registered matters. Pay the applicable registration tax and education surcharge via the court payment system before filing.
required_dossiers: Application for Corporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate from the bank
Written consent to appointment signed by each director and member
Report of corporate seal and individual seal imprint
Power of attorney to the local formation agent
Proof of payment of registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a demand for correction, remedy the stated defect within the prescribed period, usually two weeks, by filing a supplemental brief and corrected attachments. If the capital payment certificate is stale, obtain a fresh certificate from the bank. If the registry suspends or rejects the filing, file a corrected application or appeal under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act to the competent District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Registration and Communication-Selling Business Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office; Si/Gun/Gu municipal government office under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after incorporation registration, file the business registration application with the competent NTS district office to obtain the Business Registration Certificate (Saeupja Deungrok). Because the entity will operate a TikTok Shop social commerce retail business, simultaneously file the communication-selling business report with the municipal authority, identifying the platform, online store URL, operator name, corporate registry number, registered office, consumer dispute resolution mechanism, and the name of the responsible representative. This report is a registration filing rather than a discretionary permit, but it must be completed before consumer-facing sales operations begin.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters from the Court Registry
Corporate Seal Certificate
Business Registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease agreement or owner consent
Representative director identification
Communication-Selling Business Report form
TikTok Shop seller account details and platform agreement
Wise B2B corporate onboarding and KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS requests additional documentation, furnish an updated certificate of registered matters and a power of attorney appointing a local tax representative. If the municipal government returns the communication-selling report for incomplete business scope, amend the description to expressly include online social commerce retail and resubmit within the correction period. If the report is not processed within five business days, issue a formal request for deemed-confirmation under the Administrative Procedures Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Corporate Seal Management, and Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The company's chosen commercial bank Corporate Banking Division; the District Court registry for seal handling; TikTok Shop and Wise B2B compliance teams for payout onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Registered Matters, take the registered corporate seal, corporate seal certificate, and court registration extract to the bank and convert the temporary deposit account into a permanent operating account. Ensure the bank file is updated with the final board resolution and authorized signatories. Apply for and collect the Corporate Seal Certificate from the Court Registry if not already issued. Then complete the TikTok Shop seller payout onboarding and Wise B2B cross-border payment onboarding by submitting the corporate registration extract, business registration certificate, communication-selling business report, certificate of corporate seal, and completed AML questionnaires. Sign the payout authorization forms and test the settlement flow with a nominal amount.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters
Corporate Seal Certificate
Business Registration Certificate from NTS
Communication-Selling Business Report certificate or receipt
Bank account application and specimen signature card
Final board resolution approving bank signatories
TikTok Shop payout onboarding package
Wise B2B corporate onboarding application
AML and source-of-wealth questionnaire for each signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced KYC objections, submit a current board resolution, source-of-wealth statement, and certified translations of corporate documents. If TikTok Shop or Wise B2B rejects the seller package due to legal-name or address mismatch, obtain a corrected registry extract and file an updated communication-selling report. If documents are challenged as insufficient, obtain direct electronic verification letters from the Court Registry and NTS and resubmit through the provider's compliance portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure online social commerce retail under ISIC 4791; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or physical retail industrial license is required from Korea Industrial Complex Agency or any municipal industrial bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehouse, or physical store operating permit is required. The obligatory business authorizations for this entity are the National Tax Service Business Registration and the communication-selling business report under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, both of which are registration-type obligations and are addressed in the formation SOP.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment (Korea) EIA regime does not apply to office-based e-commerce operations with no physical project works.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment study, no environmental registration, and no discharge permit required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are zero process wastewater discharges, zero VOC-emitting manufacturing operations, and no hazardous waste generation from production. The company must nevertheless comply with general municipal waste obligations for e-commerce packaging and returned consumer goods under the Waste Management Act and with Korea's Extended Producer Responsibility packaging rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an office-based social commerce operation; no Civil Defense fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval for industrial facilities is required. The company should ensure the registered office premises are lawfully zoned for office/internet retail use and obtain any basic fire and electrical safety inspection required for commercial office buildings under the Fire Prevention Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at https://www.hometax.go.kr. Export customs clearance is administered by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine if the foreign non-resident entity has a Korean place of business or makes taxable supplies in Korea (including remote e-commerce sales). Step 2: If no domestic establishment, appoint a Korean tax representative as required by Korean national tax law and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Step 3: Submit the Business Registration Application to the competent district tax office (or Seoul Regional Tax Office in certain cases), attaching a certified Korean translation of the foreign registration/certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, power of attorney, the representative's proof of identity, and evidence of the domestic place of business. Step 4: File online via the Home Tax Service portal or file in person. Step 5: The NTS will verify the application and issue the statutory 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the TIN and the Korea VAT registration number. For a newly incorporated Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the domestic company must apply for its own Business Registration Number within 20 days after commencement of business; a foreign parent/investor's home-country tax ID cannot be substituted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch entity election. A domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC is automatically taxable as a separate domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, and hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed through treaty provisions, controlled foreign company rules, and domestic anti-avoidance rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold. VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of any business that supplies goods or services in Korea. The Simplified Taxpayer turnover thresholds (KRW 30,000,000 for certain services and KRW 48,000,000 for retail/wholesale trade) apply only to individual traders and do not exempt a Yuhan Hoesa LLC from VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice regime administered by the NTS through the Home Tax Service e-invoice platform. General taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices for business-to-business supplies and transmit the e-invoice data to the NTS within one day after issuance. For sales to end consumers, cash receipts are issued through the approved cash receipt system. There is no private sector fiscal stamping; the NTS performs data matching, cross-audit, and anti-fraud monitoring using the e-invoice database, cash receipt system, and pre-filled VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Domestic supplies in Korea are standard-rated at 10%; export zero-rating applies only to qualifying exports. Goods physically exported from Korea qualify for zero-rated VAT when the export is evidenced by a Korea Customs Service export declaration, the goods are actually shipped to a foreign consignee, title passes to the overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are received in foreign currency. Qualifying digital and offshore services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated when the place of supply is outside Korea (services are used or consumed abroad); the exporter must retain proof of the non-resident status of the buyer, foreign-currency remittance, and offshore usage/consumption evidence. The Korean exporter files zero-rated returns and may claim a refund of any excess input VAT through the Home Tax Service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export bill of entry) accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the foreign consignee and showing the Korean port/airport of export
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank, or the equivalent Foreign Exchange Transactions Act export-proceeds settlement record
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may demand all export evidence within the statutory assessment period (generally 5 years, extended to 7 years for fraudulent tax evasion). If zero-rating is not substantiated, the export sale is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply, VAT at 10% is assessed, statutory additional taxes and daily interest are applied, and any prior VAT refund is clawed back with interest. Deliberate false documentation or concealment can trigger aggravated additional tax up to 40% of the unpaid or unduly refunded VAT and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting as the overall Foreign Exchange Control Authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; authorized domestic foreign exchange banks are delegated as reporting and settlement institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is broadly convertible on the current account, and Korea has historically accepted IMF Article VIII obligations. Current-account settlements, including trade goods, services, royalties, and dividend remittances, are generally permitted without prior licensing provided the transaction is supported by underlying documentation and reported through an authorized foreign exchange bank to the Korean FX Information Network (FEI.NET). Capital-account transactions are more administratively controlled. Inbound foreign direct investment into the Yuhan Hoesa must be preceded by a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, filed through MOEF, KOTRA, or a delegated foreign exchange bank. The bank then issues a Foreign Investment Report Certificate that underpins capital verification. Profit remittance to a foreign shareholder is lawful but will require board approval, audited financial statements, tax clearance evidence, and proof of distributable reserves; the paying foreign exchange bank will screen for round-tripping and window-dressing. There is no blanket constitutional prohibition on capital repatriation, but the practical hurdles are evidentiary rather than convertibility-based. Korea also retains supervisory restrictions on offshore won settlement and speculative short positions, so multinational treasuries must maintain a lawful FX purpose code for each economic flow. Overall, convertibility is high for genuine business transactions, but purpose coding, reporting, and foreign-investment registration create an unavoidable administrative matrix.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank within six months from the date of export declaration. There is no mandatory surrender ratio requiring conversion of foreign currency receipts into KRW; exporters may retain the foreign currency or convert as commercially required. The deadline can be extended by prior approval from MOEF/BOK on justified grounds such as deferred payment arrangements, letter-of-credit discrepancies, or trade disputes. All export proceeds must be reported through FEI.NET and matched to the underlying export declaration to avoid administrative fines.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational KRW Account and Trade Settlement Account
Foreign Direct Investment Capital Escrow Account and FX Hedging Facility Account
TikTok Shop Payout Receivable Settlement Account in KRW
Foreign Currency Account for SWIFT MT103 Outbound Supplier Payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legal viability is LOW for primary treasury or KRW clearing. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and Payoneer are not licensed under the Korean Electronic Financial Transactions Act to hold Korean-won balances or operate as a principal settlement bank for a resident Yuhan Hoesa. They may be acceptable only as auxiliary non-KRW collection or payout gateways for cross-border marketplace receipts, provided the company maintains a full domestic banking relationship for statutory Korean won settlements, tax payments, capital verification, and FX hedging. Using a foreign EMI as the sole operational bank would also create an unauthorized foreign-exchange-business concern under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act because the EMI would be effectively intermediating KRW conversion without a domestic foreign-exchange banking license. Therefore, the blueprint requires all primary treasury liquidity, capital injection, and regulatory reporting to remain inside an authorized Korean commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-branch physical appearance is the prevailing requirement for opening the first corporate account, at least for one registered statutory officer or a duly appointed natural-person signatory with a notarized power of attorney, plus the ultimate beneficial owner if different. Remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted by Korean banks; some banks permit a video-based KYC interview after embassy or apostille notarization, but the conservative FATF-aligned interpretation requires a branch visit for the initial account. Required evidence includes the passport and Alien Registration Card, apostilled certificate of incorporation, articles of association, corporate seal registration certificate, Foreign Investment Report Certificate, board resolution appointing signatories, and source-of-funds documentation for the initial capital deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership opacity in a newly formed low-capital Yuhan Hoesa with a non-resident ultimate shareholder creates a shell-entity or corporate-strawman red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled full-chain ownership chart tracing all shares to natural persons; Foreign Investment Report Certificate from the designated Korean foreign exchange bank; capital injection evidence such as overseas bank statements, audited financial statements, or payroll records; passports, tax residence certificates, and professional reference letters for each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value TikTok Shop social-commerce revenue is inconsistent with the stated ISIC 4791 retail-trade profile and may appear as structuring, placement, or third-party settlement laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: At least six months of TikTok Shop settlement records, platform seller agreements, commission invoices, logistics and shipping manifests, inventory purchase orders, supplier invoices, and an independent reconciliation between platform gross sales, refunds, fees, and bank credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of funds through marketplace payment aggregators and fintech remittance corridors such as TikTok Shop payout rails and Wise B2B may trigger third-party payment processor suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payment-flow diagram and platform contract showing the settlement chain; Know Your Customer documentation for the payment processor; segregated account statements from the aggregator; a complete list of remitters and beneficiaries; negative media and sanctions screening results; and contractual confirmation that the company is the merchant of record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: An e-commerce-only Korean entity without visible physical substance may be suspected of being a front or conduit for cross-border criminal proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean office or warehouse lease agreement, local employment contracts, National Pension and payroll enrollment records, inventory sourcing contracts, domain and SSL registration in the company name, externally audited financial statements, corporate tax invoices, and a historical bank-account repayment and operating-expense trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the Yuhan Hoesa must be remitted in the foreign investor's name via SWIFT to a designated authorized foreign exchange bank in Korea. Before the transfer, the foreign investor must file a Foreign Investment Report with MOEF/KOTRA or the delegated bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and obtain the Foreign Investment Report Certificate. The wire instruction must reference that certificate and carry the appropriate foreign-exchange purpose code assigned by the receiving bank for investment in a domestic corporation; trade remittances and shareholder loans must never be commingled in the same MT103. Upon receipt, the foreign exchange bank converts eligible foreign currency to KRW, records the foreign investment, and issues or verifies the capital subscription documentation. The accountant then uses the bank krucial foreign investment verification statement and paid-in capital evidence to complete statutory reporting in the commercial register and audited financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border supplier payments and trade-related service disbursements, the treasury should use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with a correct FX purpose code and attached underlying invoice and contract evidence. For bulk inventory imports into the TikTok Shop retail model, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank provides payment security and documentary compliance. For lower-value, open-account transactions with established suppliers, Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are acceptable and offer moderate risk mitigation while preserving liquidity. Domestic KRW supplier and logistics payments should use the Korean financial clearing infrastructure, including KFTC and HOFINET settlement rails, rather than non-bank digital channels. All outbound payments must be reported to the Bank of Korea through the FEI.NET system; direct netting through marketplace platforms is not a substitute for properly documented financial payment rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts at an authorized Seoul foreign exchange bank, permitted only against documented underlying trade or investment exposure and with maturities aligned to expected cash flows.

Plain-vanilla KRW/USD foreign-exchange swaps for working capital management when there are both real revenue and cost legs; speculative open positions are prohibited by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to offshore counterparties or foreign investors hedging existing KRW asset exposure, only where permitted by MOEF and BOK rules and never for speculative domestic trading.
Cross-currency swaps to refinance foreign-currency liabilities on the Yuhan Hoesa balance sheet, limited to the notional and tenor of the underlying foreign-currency obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return on net income for the fiscal year, including the approved statutory financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, and the external audit report (when mandatorily audited)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax system); filing is a single point through the National Tax Service with municipal local income tax administered through the same compliance workflow
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for any other fiscal year, within three months after the close of the fiscal year, with an allowed one-month extension for enterprises filing through a certified tax agent and an additional extension for entities with foreign-source operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the under-reported tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent omission; overdue tax interest accrues at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum), plus enforced collection, asset seizure, and potential criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act. A company that repeatedly fails to file and abandons its registered office may be struck from the commercial registry by the court, causing dissolution and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax (Surtax) return calculated on the national corporate income tax base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal local government (city/county/district) through the WeTax system of the Local Tax Association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the same March 31 statutory filing deadline as the corporate income tax return for a December 31 year-end, subject to local tax ordinance extension rules which generally mirror the national corporate tax due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment or underpayment triggers a local income tax late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day (8.03% annualized); failure to file triggers a 20% unfiled/under-reported surcharge (40% for fraud), and prolonged delinquency can lead to local tax compulsory collection and seizure of bank accounts or goods.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax statutory return for the first half (January 1 - June 30), including electronic tax invoices and zero-rated export schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed and paid by July 25 immediately following the January-June tax period; where the date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the due date shifts to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without good cause attracts a 0.3% penalty per day of unpaid VAT up to 75% of the deficient tax; additional tax for failure to issue electronic tax invoices and 0.5% penalty on untimely invoice issuance; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure and possible criminal sanctions for repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax statutory return for the second half (July 1 - December 31), including final VAT reconciliation and annual electronic tax invoice submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed and paid by January 25 of the immediately following calendar year; where the date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the due date shifts to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same VAT delinquency mechanism as the first-half return: 0.3% daily surcharge capped at 75% of tax for non-filing, 0.5% surcharge for false or late tax invoices, and compulsory collection after a 1-month demand period if payment is not made.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of members and the approval of the annual financial statements, register confirmation, and appointment of auditor if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's members/shareholders in general meeting; approved minutes are kept on-site and are not filed with a regulator unless the company is subject to external audit or foreign investment report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held not later than six months after the fiscal year-end (December 31: no later than June 30 following the year); ordinary resolutions may be passed at the meeting or by unanimous written consent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting and approve the financial statements leaves the company without validly approved statutory accounts, preventing lawful dividend distribution and triggering fines under the Commercial Act (as applied to Yuhan Hoesa); if an audit is statutorily required, the auditor's report must be submitted before the financial statements can be approved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Report and foreign-invested enterprise status update (applicable if any member is a foreign investor and the entity has made a foreign investment notification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the foreign-invested enterprise's fiscal year, i.e. January 30 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; changes in foreign ownership percentage during the year must be reported within 30 days of the triggering share transfer or capital change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign-investment report may subject the foreign investor to administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and can impair the foreign-invested status tax benefits; it does not dissolve the company but may trigger revocation of incentives and KOTRA inquiry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Enforcement Decree, an independent auditor certified under Korean laws must be engaged for a Yuhan Hoesa if, as of the balance sheet date, total assets are at least KRW 12 billion; total assets are at least KRW 7 billion and debt-to-equity ratio is at least 100%; total assets are at least KRW 7 billion and revenue is at least KRW 40 billion; or the company is an entity designated by the Financial Services Commission because of public interest, listed-group affiliation, or more than 500 employees/security holders. No general headcount-only threshold exists, but the Financial Services Commission may add an auditor on systemic relevance grounds. The audit report must be prepared under K-IFRS or applicable Korean GAAP and lodged with the National Tax Service as part of the corporate income tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies required by the External Audit Act to prepare consolidated or listed-company financial statements; otherwise Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) under the Korean Accounting Standards Board; small and medium entities that do not meet the audit threshold may prepare simplified financial statements under the Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Companies, but IFRS 16/private company rules still govern leases and goodwill.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate a single central public UBO filing form for a Yuhan Hoesa. The statutory obligation is to keep the Register of Members at the registered office and to update it without delay on a transfer of membership/equity. The 30-day rule is applied in practice as the maximum window for the company to annotate the equity transfer and for the incoming member to cause the company to update its Register of Members; once recorded, the transfer is effective against the company. At each annual general meeting held within six months after the fiscal year-end, the members must confirm the register and the management must identify any ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the equity for AML/KYC refresh. Any change in the foreign investor's equity ratio must be separately reported to KOTRA within 30 days of the event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,400 per annum for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Seoul, including statutory mail handling, register maintenance, and annual meeting coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 28,000 per annum for a full statutory certification audit by a licensed Korean CPA firm, with the lower end applying to a small single-purpose retail/technology entity and the upper end applying to consolidated or foreign-parent transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% (including 10% local income tax surcharge) for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive rates from 9% to 24% plus 10% local surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA), including: (a) 50%-100% corporate tax reduction for newly established small and medium enterprises in certain business categories; (b) tax credits for R&D expenditure up to 25% of qualifying R&D costs; (c) foreign investment zones and free trade zone incentives; (d) special tax support for content, digital, and ICT businesses; (e) patent box (tax reduction for technology transfer and IP commercialisation income) and venture enterprise tax benefits; (f) COVID-19 and digital commerce transitional exemptions. Social commerce retail via TikTok Shop may qualify for SME tax reduction if the Korean entity has turnover below statutory thresholds and meets job creation criteria.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean corporate income tax return: Form 1 (법인세과세표준및세액신고서, Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Return) filed via HomeTax System (전자신고) at www.hometax.go.kr; mandatory electronic filing for corporations with gross income above statutory thresholds. Head office tax office jurisdiction: Seoul or jurisdiction based on registered headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance payments for corporations whose tax base exceeds KRW 500 million in the immediately preceding fiscal year; semi-annual early payment obligations for certain corporations under Article 63 of the Corporate Tax Act as amended)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end (usually December 31): the corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for calendar-year corporations. In case of extension granted by the Commissioner of the National Tax Service, deadline may be extended by up to 1 month (Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act), and an additional one-month extension is available as a 'want to file' extension for certain medium/small enterprises. Final payment of tax is due on the same filing deadline, while the early quarterly advance payments are due by April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31 within each fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique 10-digit Korean business registration number of the Yuhan Hoesa, including the three-digit entity type code, jurisdictional tax office code, and registration sequence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the TikTok Shop retail entity is wholly or partly owned by a non-resident, the return must contain the full legal name and foreign tax identification number of each non-resident shareholder. In case of a flow-through or consignment arrangement, supply the foreign intermediary taxpayer identification; failure to match the employer identification number with the entity seal and registration index may cause automatic rejection in HomeTax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Tax Base, Losses and Surtax (과세표준 및 결손금)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax base: gross revenue less deductible expenses, exempt income, non-deductible expenses, and unabsorbed tax losses carried forward. Field distinguishes ordinary income, capital gains, and liquidation income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the TikTok Shop revenue is sourced from short-form video live commerce targeted at Korean consumers, all gross commission income, platform subsidies, and creator-share payments must be declared. Non-resident sellers using the Korean entity as a logistic or payment conduit cannot treat the Korean entity as a 'limited risk distributor' unless transfer pricing documentation substantiates that all economically significant risks are borne and controlled in Korea. Strictly identify any foreign-sourced income from overseas TikTok Shop buyer groups to determine whether it is exempt or subject to territoriality exceptions under Article 9 of the Corporate Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Dividends and Gross-Up Income (배당금 및 의제배당)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividend income received from Korean and foreign resident companies, deemed dividends from stock redemption or capital reduction, and foreign dividend pass-through claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the Yuhan Hoesa is a shareholder of the TikTok Shop operating entity, claimed dividends must be included in gross income unless the indirect foreign tax credit is validly claimed. For any dividends streamed from the Korean LLC to a non-resident parent, the local withholding agent must report the amount in Box 3 and remit withholding tax to the National Tax Service within the statutory timeframe. A non-resident recipient claiming treaty relief must attach Form 21 for Foreign Tax Credit or DTA exemption request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Tax Adjustment and Exemptions (세무조정 및 비과세·면제)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of tax adjustments: temporary differences (accrual, depreciation, bad debt reserves), permanent differences (penalties, entertainment expense limits), statutory tax exemption provisions, and foreign exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Social commerce entities must be cautious with 'platform incentive rebates' received from TikTok Shop Singapore or ByteDance: rebates are taxable business income unless tied to the export of digital services with treaty exemption. A non-resident parent's intercompany management fees cannot be deducted unless evidence of actual service benefit is disclosed; otherwise the tax office will disallow the expense and impose a 2% documentary noncompliance surcharge. All depreciation of IT equipment, warehouse racks, and creator content production assets must follow the Corporate Tax Act Article 23 depreciation limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Additions to Tax and Penalties (가산세)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessed penalties for late filing, non-filing, underpayment, misreporting, or failure to keep proper books and records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident beneficial owner of the Korean entity has failed to obtain a Korean tax identification number, late filing penalties are doubled. Under-reporting revenue from TikTok Shop live-commerce sales with regional routing manipulation can attract a 20%-40% negligence tax penalty plus a 3% monthly understatement surcharge; criminal referral thresholds are triggered when underreporting exceeds KRW 500 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Foreign Tax Credit and Withholding Reconciliation (외국납부세액공제)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of foreign income taxes paid directly or indirectly, calculation of the foreign tax credit limit, and carryforward/carryback of excess credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For Korean-origin dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder, this line is not applicable to the Korean paying entity's return; the shareholder must separately file a Korean provisional income tax return if it also has a Korean permanent establishment. The entity must still reconcile any inbound service or royalty WHT from non-resident content-creators under the domestic sourcing rules; if the Korean entity is a single-member LLC wholly owned by a foreign resident (a 'disregarded entity' for US tax planning but taxed as a Korean domestic corporation), the foreign tax credit is capped by the Korean effective tax rate and cannot exceed 24.2% of foreign taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the corporate income tax return is filed after the statutory deadline without a valid extension: (a) unfaithful return penalty of 0.75% of the unpaid tax for the first 1 month, plus 0.15% for each additional month up to 3% of the unpaid tax; (b) non-filing penalty under the Basic Act for National Taxes: 20% of the calculated tax amount (or 10% if filed voluntarily after the due date but before tax assessment); (c) negligence penalties for false entries: 20%-40% of the unpaid tax depending on whether the misstatement is intentional (40%) or due to negligence (20%); (d) daily compound surcharge for late payment: 0.022% of the unpaid tax per day from the day after the due date until fully paid; (e) failure to keep or submit books and records: a pecuniary penalty of up to 1% of total revenue; and (f) criminal tax fraud sanctions: Article 15 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to KRW 50 million for fraudulent or unlawful means of tax evasion, elevated to imprisonment for not less than 2 years and fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax where the amount exceeds KRW 500 million, or 10 years for aggravated evasion exceeding KRW 5 billion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate income tax withholding under the Corporate Tax Act Article 73 plus 2% local income tax surcharge under the Local Tax Act Article 103-24) levied on dividends distributed by a Korean resident corporation to non-resident recipients in the absence of an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate (often 5%-15% under Korea's income tax treaties, 10% for portfolio dividends, 5% for substantial shareholding (25% or more) unless otherwise specified) or an exemption, the withholding agent must: (1) obtain a written application for tax treaty relief (Form 'Application for Tax Withholding Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty' (외국법인에 대한 조세특례 및 비과세 공제 신청서) or International Tax Form) submitted to the withholding agency (bank/paying agent) before the payment is made; (2) attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the residence country within 6 months from the date of issuance; (3) provide a beneficial ownership statement and supporting charter/ownership trail establishing the recipient is the true beneficial owner and has no contractual or legal obligation to pass the dividend to another person; (4) if the non-resident shareholder is a special-purpose vehicle, complete the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause and Main Purpose Test (MPT) under the Korea-OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) – for Korea, the Principal Purpose Test applies to all covered tax agreements unless a specific LOB exists; (5) file the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate (or equivalent) with the Ministry of Economy and Finance if the foreign investor has registered the investment; and (6) upon denial or partial denial, the non-resident recipient may file an application for refund with the District Tax Office within 3 years from the statutory filing date, attaching amended withholding receipts and proof that the withholding agent remitted the grossed-up foreign tax. If the treaty benefit is claimed after the initial withholding, the non-resident must file Form No. 27 'Refund of Excess Withheld Tax' together with a certificate from the Korean withholding agent showing the withheld amounts, a Korean transaction ledger, and a statement of facts proving the non-resident's residence, and the domestic law 3-year statute of limitation applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory withholding 22% (20% plus 2% local surcharge) on interest paid to non-residents; under most Korean treaties the rate is 10% (e.g., Korea-US treaty Article 12: 10% on interest, often reduced to 0% for governmental interest; Korea-China treaty 10%; Korea-Hong Kong DTA 10%; Korea-Singapore DTA 10% for royalties and interest; Korea-Japan treaty 10% or 5% under certain conditions). Royalties: statutory withholding 22% (20% plus 2% local surcharge) on royalties, fees for the use of industrial, commercial or scientific equipment, know-how, software licences, copyrights, films, and digital content; under treaties generally 10% or 15% (e.g., Korea-US treaty 15% for royalties, 10% for industrial/commercial equipment; Korea-China treaty 10%; Korea-Hong Kong 10% for royalties; Korea-Singapore 10%; Korea-Japan 10%). For intercompany debt interest paid by the Korean LLC to a non-resident lender, the arm's-length interest rate and thin-capitalisation rule (interest on debt exceeding 300% of equity may be disallowed without treaty claims) must be verified; the beneficial owner must satisfy the 'full-fledged interest' criteria and the treaty relief procedure identical to dividends. For royalty income tied to TikTok content and commercial software, the Korean payer must withhold on gross royalty at the statutory rate unless treaty conditions are met, and no deduction is granted to a Korean branch unless the payer is a Korean resident corporation performing the withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Articles 4-3 and 4-4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA) and Presidential Enforcement Decree Article 7: a Korean entity is required to prepare and submit (a) a Local File, (b) a Master File, and (c) a Country-by-Country Report if its total intercompany transaction value with foreign related parties in a fiscal year is KRW 10 billion or more (approximately USD 7.5 million) for the Local File obligation; threshold for Master File is KRW 50 billion; CbC Notification threshold: KRW 100 billion in consolidated group revenue. For foreign investors, a minimal annual intercompany transaction threshold of KRW 50 million applies to simplified documentation ('Summarised Intercompany Transaction Report') under ITAA Article 4-3(4); all cross-border related-party transactions (PSAs, cost-sharing, management fees, IP licence fee transactions, and online platform payout flows) must be disclosed in a separate schedule to the corporate income tax return.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Korean tax authorities apply the Authorised OECD Approach and the substance-over-form doctrine under the Corporate Tax Act Article 4 and the Framework Act on International Taxation. Under the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) adopted in connection with Korea's compliance with the EU Code of Conduct Group and the OECD BEPS standards, a Korean resident business must prove the real management and control functions – i.e., Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) – are performed in Korea through strategic decision-making, employees with technical expertise, offices and physical infrastructure. For the TikTok Shop retail entity, the following CIGA factors are critical: (a) warehouse and fulfilment staff in Korea; (b) local marketing and creator management decisions; (c) risk underwriting functions for consumer returns and refunds; (d) payment reconciliation with TikTok Shop Singapore and local payment gateways; and (e) the principal's inventory ownership and supply chain control. Having a single-member Korean LLC wholly owned by a non-resident with no local employees and all board decisions made abroad may be deemed a shell company, triggering denial of treaty benefits, penalty tax under ITAA Article 7-2 (disallowance of deductions and imputation of income to the non-resident), and administrative sanctions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the entity misrepresents its foreign investment status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Under-Reporting or Sales Suppression
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or under-reporting TikTok Shop sales revenue in the corporate income tax return, especially by routing buyer payments through a non-resident PayPal/Wise account, using a foreign company like TikTok Shop Singapore as billing principal while Korean warehouse and creator payments remain in Korea, or failing to issue tax invoices for Korean end-consumer B2C sales (and not reporting output VAT/receipts to the National Tax Service).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (조세범처벌법): imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to KRW 50 million for unlawful tax evasion; where the amount of evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment for 2 years or more and a fine of up to 5 times the tax due; where it exceeds KRW 5 billion, imprisonment for up to 10 years and a fine of up to 5 times the tax paid. Administrative penalties: National Tax Basic Act Article 47-3: 40% negligence penalty for intentional underreporting, plus a 0.022% daily late payment interest and unfaithful return penalty of 3% cap. In addition, failure to issue tax invoices under the Value-Added Tax Act Article 49 imposes a penalty of 2% of the unreported supply value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Corporate Tax Act Article 109 and the National Tax Basic Act Article 39, the representative director, financial director, and any de facto controlling shareholder of the Yuhan Hoesa are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, penalties, and surcharges where the corporation's assets are insufficient; personal assets, bank accounts, and vehicles can be seized after a demand notice. For criminal evasion, directors who engaged in the concealment or diversion of sales proceeds face criminal imprisonment of 5 years (or 10 years if the evasion exceeds KRW 5 billion), travel bans (passport revocation and immigration blacklisting) are imposed under Article 2 of the Immigration Act and the NTS 'significant taxpayer' regime, and directors may be named in NTS criminal referrals to the Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office. The veil is pierced when courts find the entity is a dummy/paper company or where the director signed false tax declarations; corporate civil damage claims by minority shareholders for breach of fiduciary duty can also arise under the Commercial Act Article 401.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Substance Failure (BEPS / ESR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean TikTok Shop retail entity as a pass-through shell: no local employees for logistics, no physical business premises, all management decisions made in Hong Kong/Singapore/US, intercompany service fees artificially allocated to a zero-tax jurisdiction, or using the Korean entity solely to obtain a business registration without carrying on actual CIGA. Also, claiming DTA relief for dividends or royalties when the recipient is not the beneficial owner and lacks economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA) and Article 7-2 (adjustment of income between related entities) empower the National Tax Service to impute income to the Korean entity, disallow intercompany charges, and apply a 10% thin-capitalisation penalty; OECD/EU Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) Pillar Two and Local Substance Rules can impose an effective minimum tax of 15%, in addition to the 22% withholding tax not being reduced under a DTA when the main purpose test fails. The Korean tax authorities may also cancel the registration of the 'head office' under the Commercial Act Article 636 and order dissolution if it is a sham. For foreign-owned SPVs, Article 9 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act imposes sanctions for false foreign-investment registration, and the NTS may deny issuance of a Tax Residency Certificate for the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In shell-company cases, courts pierce the corporate veil under the Civil Act Article 3 and Commercial Act Article 401, making directors and ultimate beneficial owners jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes, including imputed income and penalties. Directors could be subject to criminal charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 10 (making false declarations) with imprisonment up to 3 years. In addition, entrance/exit restriction (up to 2 years at the request of the National Tax Service) and blacklisting of overseas travel by the Ministry of Justice apply under Article 26 of the Foreign Travel Administration Act and Article 2 of the Immigration Act; the director's overseas assets may be traced under the Act on International Mutual Assistance in Tax Matters, and fund freeze orders are possible under Korea's AML/TF framework. Civil liability to creditors of the dissolved shell company arises under Article 171 of the Commercial Act, allowing creditors to claim against the directors' personal estates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: TP Documentation and Cross-Border Digital Commerce Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, submit, or preserve transfer pricing documentation for intercompany transactions with TikTok Shop Singapore, ByteDance group, non-resident content creators, and intra-group IP licence fees above the statutory thresholds; deliberately applying unrealistic cost-plus/markup margins, allocating residual profit to low-tax jurisdictions, or not declaring a Permanent Establishment in Korea while maintaining a warehouse, logistics team, or marketing office in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4-3(2) of the ITAA: failure to submit TP documentation may result in the tax authority's audit assessment using internally available comparables; a documentary noncompliance penalty of 2% of the value of the implicated intercompany transaction applies, and a maximum of 30% of the tax base may be additionally assessed; Article 4-4(3) CbC Report penalties: up to KRW 20 million per violation, plus daily surcharge of KRW 5,000 per day (maximum KRW 10 million) for failure to submit CbC or Master File. In addition, illegal profit-shifting can be deemed tax evasion and subject to a 40% intentional understatement penalty and criminal sanctions as tax fraud if the amount evaded exceeds KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs the corporate tax return and TP disclosures is personally liable under Article 39 of the National Tax Basic Act for 100% of the assessed additional tax, penalties, and interest where the corporate assets are deficient. Under Article 401 of the Commercial Act, directors owe fiduciary duties and may be sued for damages arising from tax mismanagement. Criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 9 (fraudulent evasion) carries imprisonment up to 5 years; for knowingly submitting false Master/Local File or CbC data with intent to mislead tax authorities, criminal fraud penalties under Article 347 of the Criminal Act (fraud) can be applied. Directors also face travel bans under NTS blacklisting, and if they use personal guarantee for corporate debt, personal bankruptcy proceedings may result. In egregious cases involving digital sales to Korean customers, the National Tax Service can coordinate with the Korean Customs Service and Internet-based payment providers to track personal accounts, leading to asset seizure and legal enforcement of criminal fines.
